Query ClickHouse as the signed-in user

Source: R/backend__clickhouse.R
oauth_db_clickhouse_api.Rd

Query ClickHouse data using the signed-in visitor's database permissions. The client sends their access token with SQL requests over HTTPS and returns data frames. No database driver is needed.

Usage

oauth_db_clickhouse_api(
  authorization,
  url,
  database = NULL,
  target = NULL,
  required_scopes = character(),
  min_valid_for = 60,
  timeout = 300,
  ca_bundle = NULL,
  session = shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()
)

Arguments

authorization

Function providing the visitor's current sign-in authorization. Pass auth$connection from shinyOAuth without parentheses. To select a saved account, use a function calling auth$connection(id).

url

HTTPS query endpoint, including its port and proxy path if needed.

database

Default database, or NULL for the user's server default.

target

Name of the service token to use in your shinyOAuth client. Named targets let one sign-in obtain tokens for different services. NULL uses the client's default token.

required_scopes

Additional OAuth permissions to check before use. Request them on the shinyOAuth client first; this check doesn't request consent or grant database privileges.

min_valid_for

Minimum remaining token lifetime, in seconds, when obtaining a token. Use 0 to accept any unexpired token.

timeout

Maximum seconds for one HTTP operation.

ca_bundle

Optional trusted CA certificate bundle path.

session

The visitor's Shiny session. Usually inferred when you create the helper inside server().

Value

A client object with these methods:

  • $query(sql, parameters = list(), raw = FALSE) returns a data frame, or the parsed server response when raw = TRUE.

  • $execute(sql, parameters = list()) runs a statement without collecting a result and invisibly returns its httr2 response.

Details

Configure your service to accept access tokens from the app's sign-in provider. Custom providers require ClickHouse Cloud Enterprise, service version 26.4 or later (26.8 for EC signing keys). The ClickHouse vignette explains the service setup.

Create the client inside server() and call its methods from render or reactive expressions. Each request uses a current token and discards results after sign-out or account changes. SQL doesn't retry automatically, since a statement may already have executed. Submitted work can continue after a timeout or sign-out.

Parameters

Use typed placeholders such as {country:String} or {id:UInt64} and a named list of R values in parameters. Values are sent separately from SQL. Character, logical, integer, numeric, Date, POSIXct and missing values are supported. Use strings for exact large integers and decimals.

R timestamps are formatted in UTC. Use DateTime('UTC') or DateTime64(6, 'UTC') in the placeholder to preserve the intended instant, including up to six fractional digits. A different SQL timezone would interpret the formatted value differently.

For arrays or tuples, wrap ClickHouse escaped-format strings in I() to preserve their encoding.

Result types

Integers of 64 bits or more and decimals stay as strings. Smaller integers and floats become R numbers, booleans become logical, and dates become Date. Timestamps keep their server string format; complex values use list columns. Empty results preserve column metadata.

Leave FORMAT clauses and output-format overrides out of SQL. Use raw = TRUE for the parsed server response, including metadata and statistics, with JSON arrays represented as R lists.

See also

vignette("clickhouse", package = "shinyOAuthDB").

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
clickhouse <- oauth_db_clickhouse_api(auth$connection,
  url = "https://example.clickhouse.cloud:8443", database = "reporting")
output$rows <- shiny::renderTable({
  clickhouse$query("SELECT id, total FROM orders WHERE country = {country:String} LIMIT 20",
    parameters = list(country = "NL"))
})
} # }
